notes: Three failures: no Emma fallibility, no James ops analogy, weakest baseline run.
Iteration 4 achieves the highest with_skill pass rate across all iterations: 95.5% (vs iter-2: 94%, iter-3: 92.5%, iter-1: 77%).
4 of 6 with_skill runs score perfect 11/11 (100%). This is unprecedented consistency.
Assertion #4 (Emma fallibility) is the primary failure mode for with_skill runs: fails in ws5 and ws6. Both runs have Emma as authoritative guide without sharing personal mistakes.
Assertion #6 (James ops analogy) passes 100% across all with_skill runs, resolving the iter-2 weakness (50%). The skill now reliably grounds James in warehouse/supplier/process optimization context.
Assertion #8 (Jonah Rhythm) fails in ws5 (implicit departure) but passes in 5/6 with_skill runs. Major improvement over iter-3.
Assertion #10 (Try With AI: 3 prompts + learning) passes 100% across ALL 8 runs. Resolved from iter-3 (33%). The skill now reliably generates exactly 3 prompts with learning explanations.
Baseline without_skill runs are strong: mean 81.8%. bl1 scores 10/11, matching some with_skill runs. The eval prompt itself is well-constructed.

The delta (+13.7%) is smaller than iter-2 (+3%) but comes from a much higher absolute baseline. With skill at 95.5% vs baseline at 81.8%, the skill provides consistent uplift on the hardest assertions (#4 fallibility, #8 Jonah Rhythm).
Emergent concepts are strong in both configurations. Every run produces at least 1 novel named framework not in the prompt. This assertion may be too easy to pass.
Cross-iteration trend: #6 went 50% -> 100% -> 100% (fixed in iter-3, held in iter-4). #10 went unstable -> 100% (fixed in iter-4). #4 remains the most variable assertion at ~67% for with_skill.
COMPARISON TO PREVIOUS ITERATIONS: Iter-1 ws=77% bl=80% delta=-3% | Iter-2 ws=94% bl=91% delta=+3% | Iter-3 ws=92.5% bl=94% delta=-1.5% | Iter-4 ws=95.5% bl=81.8% delta=+13.7%.
Iter-4 is the first iteration where the skill clearly outperforms baseline across a meaningful sample (6 ws runs vs 2 bl runs). The +13.7% delta is the largest positive delta in the series.
